new_statements.translation: B. Suprasegmental phonemes. 1. Vowel quantity is not distinctive in Kisembombo; it therefore does not allow phonological oppositions to be set up. 2. Tone. Two simple tonemes emerge from the corpus available to us: high tone and low tone. They are identified by the following oppositions: mobele 'resin tree' / mobélé 'body'; madú 'knees' / madu 'beer'; motondó 'tree (sp.)' / motondo 'line'. Although we have not established oppositions between rising and falling tone, we note nevertheless that each mora of a long vowel bears a tone.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The only suprasegmental contrasts described are lexical tone (H vs L, mora as tone-bearing unit) and (non-distinctive) vowel length; the sketch says nothing at all about word stress or accent. This is a tone-language description silent on stress, not a statement of stress position.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonology of isolated nouns/verbs (citation forms); no phrase-level prosody discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source describes Kisɛmbɔmbɔ (Kisembombo), which the author identifies as 'un parler du kizimba (ou kibinja selon les locuteurs natifs)', i.e. Binja-Sud/Zimba, Guthrie D26, Atlas linguistique du Zaïre code 432, spoken at Lukamata, Kusu, Ngungwa, Kapuli-Unga, Misenga, Calumba, Makoko (Maniema); he lists the other Kizimba dialects as kesolé, kisémolo, kyenyeménila, kikwângo and warns that intercomprehension between Kisembombo and the other Zimba dialects is 'fort malaisée'. Glottolog files both Kabungama articles under zimb1251; no separate glottocode for Kisembombo is known to me.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1 'Aperçu phonologique' (pp. 433-438) gives 7 vowels, consonants, clusters; sec. 1.B 'Les phonèmes supra-segmentaux' (p. 436) treats only vowel quantity (not distinctive) and tone (two tonemes, H and L, minimal pairs; each mora of a long vowel bears a tone). No mention of accent/stress anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent|stress|intensité|tonique over the article range: none).
